notes: Prose opening formula of the chapter; the unit is typed as a verse in the input but is a prose line. The chapter name is a derived word in -īya from aṣṭa-udara 'eight udaras', after the first words of the list in 3.

hindi: यहाँ आठ उदर, आठ मूत्राघात, आठ क्षीरदोष, आठ रेतोदोष; सात कुष्ठ, सात पिडकाएँ, सात विसर्प; छह अतीसार, छह उदावर्त, पाँच गुल्म, पाँच प्लीहदोष, पाँच कास, पाँच श्वास, पाँच हिक्का, पाँच तृष्णा, पाँच छर्दि, भोजन न करने के पाँच कारण, पाँच शिरोरोग, पाँच हृद्रोग, पाँच पाण्डुरोग, पाँच उन्माद; चार अपस्मार, चार अक्षिरोग, चार कर्णरोग, चार प्रतिश्याय, चार मुखरोग, चार ग्रहणीदोष, चार मद, चार मूर्च्छा, चार शोष, चार क्लैब्य; तीन शोफ, तीन किलास, तीन प्रकार का लोहितपित्त; दो ज्वर, दो व्रण, दो आयाम, दो गृध्रसी, दो कामला, दो प्रकार का आम, दो प्रकार का वातरक्त, दो प्रकार के अर्श; एक ऊरुस्तम्भ, एक संन्यास, एक महागद; बीस कृमिजातियाँ, बीस प्रमेह, बीस योनिव्यापद् — इस प्रकार इस संग्रह में रोगों के अड़तालीस अधिकरण गिनाए गए हैं।
english: Here, indeed, [there are] eight udaras (abdominal diseases), eight mūtrāghātas (obstructions of urine), eight defects of milk, eight defects of semen; seven kuṣṭhas, seven eruptions (piḍakā), seven visarpas; six diarrhoeas (atisāra), six udāvartas, five gulmas, five disorders of the spleen, five coughs, five dyspnoeas, five hiccups (hikkā), five morbid thirsts (tṛṣṇā), five vomitings, five grounds for not eating food, five diseases of the head, five heart diseases, five pāṇḍu diseases, five insanities; four apasmāras, four eye diseases, four ear diseases, four coryzas (pratiśyāya), four mouth diseases, four grahaṇī disorders, four intoxications (mada), four faintings, four wastings (śoṣa), four impotences (klaibya); three swellings, three kilāsas, lohitapitta of three kinds; two fevers, two wounds (vraṇa), two āyāmas, two gṛdhrasīs, two kāmalās, āma of two kinds, vātarakta of two kinds, arśas of two kinds; one ūrustambha (stiffness of the thighs), one saṃnyāsa, one mahāgada (great disease); twenty kinds of worms, twenty pramehas, twenty disorders of the female genital tract (yonivyāpad). Thus forty-eight headings of diseases have been enumerated in this compendium.

text_flags.why: aṣṭau needs a plural, and every other item of the list is plural; 4-1 has mūtrāghātā (= mūtrāghātāḥ) iti
dvididha is not a word; dvividha as in the next items and in 4-7 dvividhamāmamiti

notes: Unit 3 has śophāḥ, 4-6 has śothā (= śothāḥ): two forms of the same word for swelling, both kept. mūrcchāyāḥ (here and in 4-5) is printed as the m. plural of mūrcchāya, not of f. mūrcchā; kept as printed. āma here is taken as n. (dvividham agrees in n.); āma is m. or n. elsewhere. Disease names (kuṣṭha, visarpa, gulma, pāṇḍu, apasmāra, grahaṇī, kilāsa, lohitapitta, āyāma, gṛdhrasī, kāmalā, āma, vātarakta, arśas, saṃnyāsa, prameha, yonivyāpad) kept in Sanskrit. The count of forty-eight is the number of headings (groups), checked: 4 groups of eight, 3 of seven, 2 of six, 12 of five, 10 of four, 3 of three, 8 of two, 3 of one, 3 of twenty = 48, as also stated in verses 8 and 9.
lines_deva: इह खल्व् अष्टाव् उदराणि, अष्टौ मूत्राघातः, अष्टौ क्षीरदोषाः, अष्टौ रेतोदोषाः; सप्त कुष्ठानि, सप्त पिडकाः, सप्त विसर्पाः; षडतीसाराः, षडुदावर्ताः, पञ्च गुल्माः, पञ्च प्लीहदोषाः, पञ्च कासाः, पञ्च श्वासाः, पञ्च हिक्काः, पञ्च तृष्णाः, पञ्च छर्दयः, पञ्च भक्तस्यानशनस्थानानि, पञ्च शिरोरोगाः, पञ्च हृद्रोगाः, पञ्च पाण्डुरोगाः, पञ्चोन्मादाः; चत्वारोऽपस्माराः, चत्वारोऽक्षिरोगाः, चत्वारः कर्णरोगाः, चत्वारः प्रतिश्यायाः, चत्वारो मुखरोगाः, चत्वारो ग्रहणीदोषाः, चत्वारो मदाः, चत्वारो मूर्च्छायाः, चत्वारः शोषाः, चत्वारि क्लैब्यानि; त्रयः शोफाः, त्रीणि किलासानि, त्रिविधं लोहितपित्तं; द्वौ ज्वरौ, द्वौ व्रणौ, द्वावायामौ, द्वे गृध्रस्यौ, द्वे कामले, द्विदिधमामं, द्विविधं वातरक्तं, द्विविधान्य् अर्शांसि; एक ऊरुस्तम्भः, एकः संन्यासः, एको महागदः; विंशतिः क्रिमिजातयः, विंशतिः प्रमेहाः, विंशतिर् योनिव्यापदः; इत्य् अष्टचत्वारिंशद् रोगाधिकरणान्य् अस्मिन् संग्रहे समुद्दिष्टानि
lines_iast: iha khalv aṣṭāv udarāṇi, aṣṭau mūtrāghātaḥ, aṣṭau kṣīradoṣāḥ, aṣṭau retodoṣāḥ; sapta kuṣṭhāni, sapta piḍakāḥ, sapta visarpāḥ; ṣaḍatīsārāḥ, ṣaḍudāvartāḥ, pañca gulmāḥ, pañca plīhadoṣāḥ, pañca kāsāḥ, pañca śvāsāḥ, pañca hikkāḥ, pañca tṛṣṇāḥ, pañca chardayaḥ, pañca bhaktasyānaśanasthānāni, pañca śirorogāḥ, pañca hṛdrogāḥ, pañca pāṇḍurogāḥ, pañconmādāḥ; catvāro'pasmārāḥ, catvāro'kṣirogāḥ, catvāraḥ karṇarogāḥ, catvāraḥ pratiśyāyāḥ, catvāro mukharogāḥ, catvāro grahaṇīdoṣāḥ, catvāro madāḥ, catvāro mūrcchāyāḥ, catvāraḥ śoṣāḥ, catvāri klaibyāni; trayaḥ śophāḥ, trīṇi kilāsāni, trividhaṃ lohitapittaṃ; dvau jvarau, dvau vraṇau, dvāvāyāmau, dve gṛdhrasyau, dve kāmale, dvididhamāmaṃ, dvividhaṃ vātaraktaṃ, dvividhāny arśāṃsi; eka ūrustambhaḥ, ekaḥ saṃnyāsaḥ, eko mahāgadaḥ; viṃśatiḥ krimijātayaḥ, viṃśatiḥ pramehāḥ, viṃśatir yonivyāpadaḥ; ity aṣṭacatvāriṃśad rogādhikaraṇāny asmin saṃgrahe samuddiṣṭāni

hindi: इन्हें हम उद्देश के क्रम से स्पष्ट करेंगे — 'आठ उदर': वात, पित्त, कफ, सन्निपात, प्लीहा, बद्ध, छिद्र और दक उदर; 'आठ मूत्राघात': वात, पित्त, कफ, सन्निपात, अश्मरी, शर्करा, शुक्र और शोणित से उत्पन्न; 'आठ क्षीरदोष': विवर्णता, दुर्गन्ध, विरसता, पिच्छिलता, झाग का जमाव, रूक्षता, गुरुता और अतिस्निग्धता; 'आठ रेतोदोष': पतला, सूखा, झागदार, अश्वेत, सड़ा हुआ, अति पिच्छिल, अन्य धातुओं से मिला हुआ और नीचे बैठने वाला।
english: These we shall specify in the order of the enumeration. 'Eight udaras': the udaras of Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, sannipāta (all three combined), the spleen, obstruction (baddha), perforation (chidra) and water (daka). 'Eight obstructions of urine': those born of Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, sannipāta, stone (aśmarī), gravel (śarkarā), semen and blood. 'Eight defects of milk': discoloration, bad smell, bad taste, sliminess, massing of froth, roughness, heaviness and excess of unctuousness. 'Eight defects of semen': [semen that is] thin, dry, frothy, not white, putrid, very slimy, mixed with other dhātus, and sinking.
notes: sannipāta = the combination of all three doṣas. daka = udaka 'water' (dakodara = water-udara). baddha 'bound, obstructed' and chidra 'hole, perforation' are given their literal meanings. avasādi (from ava-√sad) is taken as 'sinking (to the bottom)'; it could also mean 'depressed, weak'. kṣīra = milk, as printed. The section number (1) is the edition's.
lines_deva: एतानि यथोद्देशमभिनिर्देक्ष्यामः--- अष्टावुदराणीति वातपित्तकफसन्निपातप्लीहबद्धच्छिद्रदकोदराणि, अष्टौ मूत्राघाता इति वातपित्तकफसन्निपाताश्मरीशर्कराशुक्रशोणितजाः, अष्टौ क्षीरदोषा इति वैवर्ण्यं वैगन्ध्यं वैरस्यं पैच्छिल्यं फेनसङ्घातो रौक्ष्यं गौरवमतिस्नेहश्च, अष्टौ रेतोदोषा इति तनु शुष्कं फेनिलमश्वेतं पूत्यतिपिच्छलमन्यधातूपहितमवसादि च (१);
lines_iast: etāni yathoddeśamabhinirdekṣyāmaḥ--- aṣṭāvudarāṇīti vātapittakaphasannipātaplīhabaddhacchidradakodarāṇi, aṣṭau mūtrāghātā iti vātapittakaphasannipātāśmarīśarkarāśukraśoṇitajāḥ, aṣṭau kṣīradoṣā iti vaivarṇyaṃ vaigandhyaṃ vairasyaṃ paicchilyaṃ phenasaṅghāto raukṣyaṃ gauravamatisnehaśca, aṣṭau retodoṣā iti tanu śuṣkaṃ phenilamaśvetaṃ pūtyatipicchalamanyadhātūpahitamavasādi ca (1);

hindi: 'सात कुष्ठ': कपाल, उदुम्बर, मण्डल, ऋष्यजिह्व, पुण्डरीक, सिध्म और काकण; 'सात पिडकाएँ': शराविका, कच्छपिका, जालिनी, सर्षपी, अलजी, विनता और विद्रधी; 'सात विसर्प': वात, पित्त, कफ, अग्नि, कर्दमक, ग्रन्थि और सन्निपात नाम वाले।
english: 'Seven kuṣṭhas': kapāla, udumbara, maṇḍala, ṛṣyajihva, puṇḍarīka, sidhma and kākaṇa. 'Seven eruptions': śarāvikā, kacchapikā, jālinī, sarṣapī, alajī, vinatā and vidradhī. 'Seven visarpas': those named Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, agni (fire), kardamaka, granthi and sannipāta.
notes: Names kept in Sanskrit. Literal meanings of the kuṣṭha names: kapāla 'potsherd', udumbara 'fig', maṇḍala 'circle', ṛṣyajihva 'antelope's tongue', puṇḍarīka 'lotus', kākaṇa (unclear, kept). kardamaka 'muddy', granthi 'knot'.
lines_deva: सप्त कुष्ठानीति कपालोदुम्बरमण्डलर्ष्यजिह्वपुण्डरीकसिध्मकाकणानि, सप्त पिडका इति शराविका कच्छपिका जालिनी सर्षप्यलजी विनता विद्रधी च, सप्त विसर्पा इति वातपित्तकफाग्निकर्दमकग्रन्थिसन्निपाताख्याः (२);
lines_iast: sapta kuṣṭhānīti kapālodumbaramaṇḍalarṣyajihvapuṇḍarīkasidhmakākaṇāni, sapta piḍakā iti śarāvikā kacchapikā jālinī sarṣapyalajī vinatā vidradhī ca, sapta visarpā iti vātapittakaphāgnikardamakagranthisannipātākhyāḥ (2);

hindi: 'छह अतीसार': वात, पित्त, कफ, सन्निपात, भय और शोक से उत्पन्न; 'छह उदावर्त': वात, मूत्र, पुरीष, शुक्र, छर्दि और छींक से उत्पन्न।
english: 'Six diarrhoeas': those born of Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, sannipāta, fear and grief. 'Six udāvartas': those born of flatus (vāta), urine, faeces, semen, vomiting and sneezing.
notes: In the udāvarta list vāta is taken as flatus, since it stands among the bodily discharges. The text says only 'born of' these; it does not say here whether their suppression is meant.
lines_deva: षडतीसारा इति वातपित्तकफसन्निपातभयशोकजाः, षडुदावर्ता इति वातमूत्रपुरीषशुक्रच्छर्दिक्षवथुजाः (३);

hindi: 'पाँच गुल्म': वात, पित्त, कफ, सन्निपात और शोणित से उत्पन्न; 'पाँच प्लीहदोष' गुल्मों के समान व्याख्यात हैं; 'पाँच कास': वात, पित्त, कफ, क्षत और क्षय से उत्पन्न; 'पाँच श्वास': महा, ऊर्ध्व, छिन्न, तमक और क्षुद्र; 'पाँच हिक्का': महती, गम्भीरा, व्यपेता, क्षुद्रा और अन्नजा; 'पाँच तृष्णा': वात, पित्त, आम, क्षय और उपसर्ग स्वरूप वाली; 'पाँच छर्दि': अप्रिय विषयों के संयोग से उत्पन्न और वात, पित्त, कफ तथा सन्निपात की अधिकता से उठने वाली; 'भोजन न करने के पाँच कारण': वात, पित्त, कफ, सन्निपात और द्वेष; 'पाँच शिरोरोग' पूर्व उद्देश को साथ लेकर वात, पित्त, कफ, सन्निपात और कृमि से उत्पन्न; 'पाँच हृद्रोग' शिरोरोगों के समान व्याख्यात हैं; 'पाँच पाण्डुरोग': वात, पित्त, कफ, सन्निपात और मिट्टी खाने से उत्पन्न; 'पाँच उन्माद': वात, पित्त, कफ, सन्निपात और आगन्तु कारण वाले।
english: 'Five gulmas': those born of Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, sannipāta and blood. 'Five disorders of the spleen' are explained by the gulmas. 'Five coughs': those born of Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, injury (kṣata) and wasting (kṣaya). 'Five dyspnoeas': the great, the upward, the interrupted, tamaka and the minor. 'Five hiccups': the great (mahatī), the deep (gambhīrā), the intermittent (vyapetā), the minor (kṣudrā) and the food-born (annajā). 'Five morbid thirsts': those of the nature of Vāta, Pitta, āma, wasting and secondary affection (upasarga). 'Five vomitings': one born of contact with disliked objects, and those arising from the predominance of Vāta, Pitta, Kapha and sannipāta. 'Five grounds for not eating food': Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, sannipāta and aversion. 'Five diseases of the head': taking together the former enumeration, those born of Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, sannipāta and worms. 'Five heart diseases' are explained by the diseases of the head. 'Five pāṇḍu diseases': those born of Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, sannipāta and eating clay. 'Five insanities': those caused by Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, sannipāta and exogenous factors (āgantu).
notes: 'Explained by the gulmas' / 'by the diseases of the head': the spleen disorders follow the same five-fold division as the gulmas, and the heart diseases the same as the head diseases. pūrvoddeśam abhisamasya (abs. of abhi-sam-√as, 'having put together') is read as 'taking together the earlier listing' (the Vāta-Pitta-Kapha-sannipāta series); exact sense medium. vyapetā (vi-apa-√i, 'gone apart') is rendered 'intermittent'; it could also mean 'separated, irregular'. upasarga is rendered 'secondary affection' (literally 'that which attaches itself'); the precise sense is not stated here. kṣudrānnajā is split kṣudrā + annajā, as the count of five requires. tamaka kept Sanskrit.
lines_deva: पञ्च गुल्मा इति वातपित्तकफसन्निपातशोणितजाः, पञ्च प्लीहदोषा इति गुल्मैर्व्याख्याताः, पञ्च कासा इति वातपित्तकफक्षतक्षयजाः, पञ्च श्वासा इति महोर्ध्वच्छिन्नतमकक्षुद्राः, पञ्च हिक्का इति महती गम्भीरा व्यपेता क्षुद्रान्नजा च, पञ्च तृष्णा इति वातपित्तामक्षयोपसर्गात्मिकाः, पञ्च छर्दय इति द्विष्टार्थसंयोगजा वातपित्तकफसन्निपातोद्रेकोत्थाश्च, पञ्च भक्तस्यानशनस्थानानीति वातपित्तकफसन्निपातद्वेषाः, पञ्च शिरोरोगा इति पूर्वोद्देशमभिसमस्य वातपित्तकफसन्निपातक्रिमिजाः, पञ्च हृद्रोगा इति शिरोरोगैर्व्याख्याताः, पञ्च पाण्डुरोगा इति वातपित्तकफसन्निपातमृद्भक्षणजाः, पञ्चोन्मादा इति वातपित्तकफसन्निपातागन्तुनिमित्ताः (४);
lines_iast: pañca gulmā iti vātapittakaphasannipātaśoṇitajāḥ, pañca plīhadoṣā iti gulmairvyākhyātāḥ, pañca kāsā iti vātapittakaphakṣatakṣayajāḥ, pañca śvāsā iti mahordhvacchinnatamakakṣudrāḥ, pañca hikkā iti mahatī gambhīrā vyapetā kṣudrānnajā ca, pañca tṛṣṇā iti vātapittāmakṣayopasargātmikāḥ, pañca chardaya iti dviṣṭārthasaṃyogajā vātapittakaphasannipātodrekotthāśca, pañca bhaktasyānaśanasthānānīti vātapittakaphasannipātadveṣāḥ, pañca śirorogā iti pūrvoddeśamabhisamasya vātapittakaphasannipātakrimijāḥ, pañca hṛdrogā iti śirorogairvyākhyātāḥ, pañca pāṇḍurogā iti vātapittakaphasannipātamṛdbhakṣaṇajāḥ, pañconmādā iti vātapittakaphasannipātāgantunimittāḥ (4);

words.gloss: caused by Vāta, Pitta, Kapha and sannipāta

words.gram: m. nom. pl., past part. vi-ā-√khyā

words.gloss: born of over-exertion, suppression, depletion and irregular eating

hindi: 'चार अपस्मार': वात, पित्त, कफ और सन्निपात के कारण वाले; चार अक्षिरोग, चार कर्णरोग, चार प्रतिश्याय, चार मुखरोग, चार ग्रहणीदोष, चार मद और चार मूर्च्छा — ये अपस्मारों के समान व्याख्यात हैं; 'चार शोष': साहस, सन्धारण, क्षय और विषम भोजन से उत्पन्न; 'चार क्लैब्य': बीज के उपघात से, ध्वज के भङ्ग से, जरा से और शुक्र के क्षय से।
english: 'Four apasmāras': those caused by Vāta, Pitta, Kapha and sannipāta. Four eye diseases, four ear diseases, four coryzas, four mouth diseases, four grahaṇī disorders, four intoxications and four faintings are explained by the apasmāras. 'Four wastings': those born of over-exertion (sāhasa), suppression (sandhāraṇa), depletion (kṣaya) and irregular eating. 'Four impotences': from damage to the seed, from breakdown of the penis (dhvaja), from old age, and from depletion of semen.
notes: 'Explained by the apasmāras' = these seven groups follow the same four-fold division (Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, sannipāta). sāhasa literally 'rash or violent act', here taken as over-exertion; sandhāraṇa 'holding back', taken as suppression (of urges), which the text does not spell out. mūrcchāyāḥ kept as printed (m. pl. of mūrcchāya); see unit 3.
lines_deva: चत्वारोऽपस्मारा इति वातपित्तकफसन्निपातनिमित्ताः, चत्वारोऽक्षिरोगाश्चत्वारः कर्णरोगाश्चत्वारः प्रतिश्यायाश्चत्वारो मुखरोगाश्चत्वारो ग्रहणीदोषाश्चत्वारो मदाश्चत्वारो मूर्च्छाया इत्यपस्मारैर्व्याख्याताः, चत्वारः शोषा इति साहससन्धारणक्षयविषमाशनजाः, चत्वारि क्लैब्यानीति बीजोपघाताद्ध्वजभङ्गाज्जरायाः शुक्रक्षयाच्च (५);
lines_iast: catvāro'pasmārā iti vātapittakaphasannipātanimittāḥ, catvāro'kṣirogāścatvāraḥ karṇarogāścatvāraḥ pratiśyāyāścatvāro mukharogāścatvāro grahaṇīdoṣāścatvāro madāścatvāro mūrcchāyā ityapasmārairvyākhyātāḥ, catvāraḥ śoṣā iti sāhasasandhāraṇakṣayaviṣamāśanajāḥ, catvāri klaibyānīti bījopaghātāddhvajabhaṅgājjarāyāḥ śukrakṣayācca (5);

words.gloss: caused by Vāta, Pitta and Kapha (śleṣman)

hindi: 'तीन शोथ': वात, पित्त और श्लेष्मा के कारण वाले; 'तीन किलास': लाल, ताम्र और श्वेत; 'तीन प्रकार का लोहितपित्त': ऊर्ध्वभाग, अधोभाग और उभयभाग।
english: 'Three swellings': those caused by Vāta, Pitta and Kapha (śleṣman). 'Three kilāsas': red, coppery and white. 'Lohitapitta of three kinds': going upward, going downward and going both ways.
notes: ūrdhvabhāga etc. are read as bahuvrīhis, 'whose course (bhāga, side) is upward / downward / both'. śotha here = śopha of unit 3.
lines_deva: त्रयः शोथा इति वातपित्तश्लेष्मनिमित्ताः, त्रीणि किलासानीति रक्तताम्रशुक्लानि, त्रिविधं लोहितपित्तमिति ऊर्ध्वभागमधोभागमुभयभागं च (६);
lines_iast: trayaḥ śothā iti vātapittaśleṣmanimittāḥ, trīṇi kilāsānīti raktatāmraśuklāni, trividhaṃ lohitapittamiti ūrdhvabhāgamadhobhāgamubhayabhāgaṃ ca (6);

hindi: 'दो ज्वर': उष्ण की इच्छा वाला और शीत से उत्पन्न, तथा शीत की इच्छा वाला और उष्ण से उत्पन्न; 'दो व्रण': निज और आगन्तुज; 'दो आयाम': बाह्य और आभ्यन्तर; 'दो गृध्रसी': वात से और वात-कफ से; 'दो कामला': कोष्ठ के आश्रय वाली और शाखा के आश्रय वाली; 'दो प्रकार का आम': अलसक और विसूचिका; 'दो प्रकार का वातरक्त': गम्भीर और उत्तान; 'दो प्रकार के अर्श': शुष्क और आर्द्र।
english: 'Two fevers': one that desires heat and arises from cold, and one that desires cold and arises from heat. 'Two wounds': the endogenous and the exogenous. 'Two āyāmas': the external and the internal. 'Two gṛdhrasīs': from Vāta, and from Vāta and Kapha. 'Two kāmalās': one based in the trunk (koṣṭha) and one based in the periphery (śākhā). 'Āma of two kinds': alasaka and visūcikā. 'Vātarakta of two kinds': deep and superficial. 'Arśas of two kinds': dry and moist.
notes: vātakaphāt is read as a samāhāra dvandva (n. abl. sg.). āyāma literally 'stretching, extension'; kept Sanskrit. alasaka and visūcikā kept Sanskrit.
lines_deva: द्वौ ज्वराविति उष्णाभिप्रायः शीतसमुत्थश्च शीताभिप्रायश्चोष्णसमुत्थः, द्वौ व्रणाविति निजश्चागन्तुजश्च, द्वावायामाविति बाह्यश्चाभ्यन्तरश्च, द्वे गृध्रस्याविति वाताद्वातकफाच्च, द्वे कामले इति कोष्ठाश्रया शाखाश्रया च, द्विविधमाममिति अलसको विसूचिका च, द्विविधं वातरक्तमिति गम्भीरमुत्तानं च, द्विविधान्यर्शांसीति शुष्काण्यार्द्राणि च (७);
lines_iast: dvau jvarāviti uṣṇābhiprāyaḥ śītasamutthaśca śītābhiprāyaścoṣṇasamutthaḥ, dvau vraṇāviti nijaścāgantujaśca, dvāvāyāmāviti bāhyaścābhyantaraśca, dve gṛdhrasyāviti vātādvātakaphācca, dve kāmale iti koṣṭhāśrayā śākhāśrayā ca, dvividhamāmamiti alasako visūcikā ca, dvividhaṃ vātaraktamiti gambhīramuttānaṃ ca, dvividhānyarśāṃsīti śuṣkāṇyārdrāṇi ca (7);

words.gloss: arising from āma and the three doṣas
of the nature of the three doṣas
attachment to what is not true

hindi: 'एक ऊरुस्तम्भ': आम और तीनों दोषों से उत्पन्न; 'एक संन्यास': तीनों दोषों के स्वरूप वाला, मन और शरीर में अधिष्ठित; 'एक महागद': अतत्त्व में अभिनिवेश।
english: 'One ūrustambha': arising from āma and the three doṣas. 'One saṃnyāsa': of the nature of the three doṣas, seated in mind and body. 'One mahāgada (great disease)': atattvābhiniveśa (attachment to what is not true).
notes: āmatridoṣa is read as a dvandva 'āma and the three doṣas'; it could also be read 'the three doṣas with āma'. atattva = 'non-reality, what is not the truth'; abhiniveśa = 'fixed attachment, obstinate adherence'.
lines_deva: एक ऊरुस्तम्भ इत्यामत्रिदोषसमुत्थः, एकः संन्यास इति त्रिदोषात्मको मनःशरीराधिष्ठानः, एको महागद इति अतत्त्वाभिनिवेशः (८);
lines_iast: eka ūrustambha ityāmatridoṣasamutthaḥ, ekaḥ saṃnyāsa iti tridoṣātmako manaḥśarīrādhiṣṭhānaḥ, eko mahāgada iti atattvābhiniveśaḥ (8);

words.gloss: disorders of the female genital tract

hindi: 'बीस कृमिजातियाँ': यूका और पिपीलिका — ये दो प्रकार के बाहरी मल से उत्पन्न; केशाद, लोमाद, लोमद्वीप, सौरस, औदुम्बर और जन्तुमाता — ये छह शोणित से उत्पन्न; अन्त्राद, उदरावेष्ट, हृदयाद, चुरु, दर्भपुष्प, सौगन्धिक और महागुद — ये सात कफ से उत्पन्न; ककेरुक, मकेरुक, लेलिह, सशूलक और सौसुराद — ये पाँच पुरीष से उत्पन्न। 'बीस प्रमेह': उदकमेह, इक्षुबालिकारसमेह, सान्द्रमेह, सान्द्रप्रसादमेह, शुक्लमेह, शुक्रमेह, शीतमेह, शनैर्मेह, सिकतामेह और लालामेह — ये दस श्लेष्मा के कारण वाले; क्षारमेह, कालमेह, नीलमेह, लोहितमेह, मञ्जिष्ठामेह, हरिद्रामेह, हस्तिमेह और मधुमेह — ये चार वात के कारण वाले; इस प्रकार बीस प्रमेह हैं। 'बीस योनिव्यापद्': वातिकी, पैत्तिकी, श्लेष्मिकी और सान्निपातिकी — ये चार दोषों से उत्पन्न; शेष सोलह दोष और दूष्य के संसर्ग तथा प्रकृति के निर्देशों से बताई जाती हैं, जैसे — रक्तयोनि, अरजस्का, अचरणा, अतिचरणा, प्राक्चरणा, उपप्लुता, परिप्लुता, उदावर्तिनी, कर्णिनी, पुत्रघ्नी, अन्तर्मुखी, सूचीमुखी, शुष्का, वामिनी, षण्ढयोनि और महायोनि; इस प्रकार बीस योनिव्यापद् होती हैं।
english: 'Twenty kinds of worms': lice (yūkā) and pipīlikās, these two kinds born of external dirt; keśāda, lomāda, lomadvīpa, saurasa, audumbara and jantumātṛ, these six born of blood; antrāda, udarāveṣṭa, hṛdayāda, curu, darbhapuṣpa, saugandhika and mahāguda, these seven born of Kapha; kakeruka, makeruka, leliha, saśūlaka and sausurāda, these five born of faeces. 'Twenty pramehas': udakameha, ikṣubālikārasameha, sāndrameha, sāndraprasādameha, śuklameha, śukrameha, śītameha, śanairmeha, sikatāmeha and lālāmeha, these ten caused by Kapha (śleṣman); kṣārameha, kālameha, nīlameha, lohitameha, mañjiṣṭhāmeha, haridrāmeha, hastimeha and madhumeha, these four caused by Vāta: thus [there are] twenty pramehas. 'Twenty disorders of the female genital tract': the Vātika, Paittika, Śleṣmika and Sānnipātika, these four born of the doṣas; the remaining sixteen are designated by their naming after the combination of doṣa and dūṣya and after their nature, namely: raktayoni, arajaskā, acaraṇā, aticaraṇā, prākcaraṇā, upaplutā, pariplutā, udāvartinī, karṇinī, putraghnī, antarmukhī, sūcīmukhī, śuṣkā, vāminī, ṣaṇḍhayoni and mahāyoni: thus there are twenty disorders of the female genital tract.

text_flags.why: krami is not a word; unit 3 has krimijātayaḥ for the same heading

notes: Worm and prameha names kept in Sanskrit with literal glosses only; no identifications. yūkā (louse) and pipīlikā (literally 'ant') are given their word meanings only; yūkā is kept as printed (f. nom. sg., collective; a plural yūkāḥ would keep its visarga before p). jantumātaraḥ is the nom. pl. of jantumātṛ (f.). Counting: worms 2 + 6 + 7 + 5 = 20, as stated; yonivyāpad 4 + 16 = 20, sixteen names given. Prameha count as printed: ten names summed as daśa śleṣmanimittāḥ, then eight names (kṣāra, kāla, nīla, lohita, mañjiṣṭhā, haridrā, hasti, madhu) summed as catvāro vātanimittāḥ: eighteen names in all against the twenty stated twice, and no Pitta group is named; the translation follows the print. ikṣubālikārasa kept as printed (bālikā; b/v spelling not flagged); bālikā cannot mean 'girl' here, ikṣubālikā is read as one plant name. śleṣmikī is kept as printed (vātikī and paittikī have vṛddhi, this form does not). doṣadūṣyasaṃsargaprakṛtinirdeśaiḥ: the analysis 'designations by the combination of doṣa and dūṣya, and by nature (prakṛti)' is medium; prakṛti could also mean the nature of the woman. The f. nom. pl. avaśiṣṭāḥ agrees with yonivyāpadaḥ (f.).
lines_deva: विंशतिः क्रमिजातय इति यूका पिपीलिकाश्चेति द्विविधा बहिर्मलजाः, केशादा लोमादा लोमद्वीपाः सौरसा औदुम्बरा जन्तुमातरश्चेति षट् शोणितजाः, अन्त्रादा उदरावेष्टा हृदयादाश्चुरवो दर्भपुष्पाः सौगन्धिका महागुदाश्चेति सप्त कफजाः, ककेरुका मकेरुका लेलिहाः सशूलकाः सौसुरादाश्चेति पञ्च पुरीषजाः; विंशतिः प्रमेहा इत्युदकमेहश्चेक्षुबालिकारसमेहश्च सान्द्रमेहश्च सान्द्रप्रसादमेहश्च शुक्लमेहश्च शुक्रमेहश्च शीतमेहश्च शनैर्मेहश्च सिकतामेहश्च लालामेहश्चेति दश श्लेष्मनिमित्ताः, क्षारमेहश्च कालमेहश्च नीलमेहश्च लोहितमेहश्च मञ्जिष्ठामेहश्च हरिद्रामेहश्च हस्तिमेहश्च मधुमेहश्चेति चत्वारो वातनिमित्ताः, इति विंशतिः प्रमेहाः; विंशतिर् योनिव्यापद इति वातिकी पैत्तिकी श्लेष्मिकी सान्निपातिकी चेति चतस्रो दोषजाः, दोषदूष्यसंसर्गप्रकृतिनिर्देशैरवशिष्टाः षोडश निर्दिश्यन्ते, तद्यथा --- रक्तयोनिश्चारजस्का चाचरणा चातिचरणा च प्राक्चरणा चोपप्लुता च परिप्लुता चोदावर्तिनी च कर्णिनी च पुत्रघ्नी चान्तर्मुखी च सूचीमुखी च शुष्का च वामिनी च षण्ढयोनिश् च महायोनिश्चेति विंशतिर् योनिव्यापदो भवन्ति (९);

hindi: सभी निज विकार वात, पित्त और कफ को छोड़कर अन्य किसी से उत्पन्न ही नहीं होते; जैसे पक्षी पूरे दिन उड़ता रहकर भी अपनी छाया का अतिक्रमण नहीं करता, वैसे ही अपनी धातुओं की विषमता के कारण होने वाले सभी विकार वात, पित्त और कफ का अतिक्रमण नहीं करते।
english: All endogenous disorders indeed arise from nothing other than Vāta, Pitta and Kapha. Just as a bird, though flying about the whole day, does not go beyond its own shadow, so all disorders caused by imbalance of one's own dhātus do not go beyond Vāta, Pitta and Kapha.

hindi: फिर बुद्धिमान् लोग वात, पित्त और श्लेष्मा के स्थान, संस्थान और प्रकृति के विशेषों को भली-भाँति देखकर, उन्हीं के स्वरूप वाले सब विकारों को भी उन्हीं (दोषों) के रूप में बताते हैं।
english: Further, the intelligent, having carefully observed the particulars of site, form and nature of Vāta, Pitta and Kapha (śleṣman), designate all disorders too, which have these as their nature, as just those [doṣas].
notes: tān eva is read as the predicate ('as just those', i.e. as Vāta, Pitta, Kapha); it could also be read with sarvavikārān, 'designate all those disorders'. saṃsthāna is rendered 'form'; it can also mean 'disposition, arrangement'.

english: And here there are two: The many groups of disorders in the body that are born from imbalance of one's own dhātus are not separate from Pitta, Kapha and Vāta (anila); but the exogenous ones are indeed distinct from them.
notes: bhavataḥ (dual) refers to the two verses 6 and 7. Upajāti metre (11 syllables a quarter). pittakaphānilebhya = -bhyaḥ before a vowel (visarga dropped). tataḥ is read as 'from them' (from the doṣas).

hindi: आगन्तु विकार निज विकार का अनुगमन करता है, और इसी प्रकार बढ़ा हुआ निज विकार आगन्तु का भी; वहाँ अनुबन्ध और प्रकृति को भली-भाँति जानकर फिर कर्म आरम्भ करे।
english: The exogenous [disorder] follows the endogenous disorder, and likewise the endogenous, when increased, follows the exogenous too. There, having correctly known the secondary (anubandha) and the primary (prakṛti), one should then begin action (karma).
notes: anubandha = what is attached, the secondary or associated element; prakṛti here = the primary, principal element (not 'normal state'). karma is the treatment to be undertaken. Upajāti metre.
